verses.html: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of Asaph. Sing aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.
verses.text: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of Asaph. Sing aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.
verses.title: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of Asaph.
verses.titleHtml: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of Asaph.

verses.html: Take a psalm, and bring hither the timbrel, the pleasant harp with the psaltery.
verses.text: Take a psalm, and bring hither the timbrel, the pleasant harp with the psaltery.

verses.html: Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day.
verses.text: Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day.

verses.html: For this was a statute for Israel, and a law of the God of Jacob.
verses.text: For this was a statute for Israel, and a law of the God of Jacob.

verses.html: This he ordained in Joseph for a testimony, when he went out through the land of Egypt: where I heard a language that I understood not.
verses.text: This he ordained in Joseph for a testimony, when he went out through the land of Egypt: where I heard a language that I understood not.

verses.html: I removed his shoulder from the burden: his hands were delivered from the pots.
verses.text: I removed his shoulder from the burden: his hands were delivered from the pots.

verses.html: Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee; I answered thee in the secret place of thunder: I proved thee at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
verses.text: Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee; I answered thee in the secret place of thunder: I proved thee at the waters of Meribah. Selah.

verses.html: Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me;
verses.text: Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me;

verses.html: There shall no strange god be in thee; neither shalt thou worship any strange god.
verses.text: There shall no strange god be in thee; neither shalt thou worship any strange god.

verses.html: I am the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.
verses.text: I am the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.

verses.html: But my people would not hearken to my voice; and Israel would none of me.
verses.text: But my people would not hearken to my voice; and Israel would none of me.

verses.html: So I gave them up unto their own hearts' lust: and they walked in their own counsels.
verses.text: So I gave them up unto their own hearts' lust: and they walked in their own counsels.

verses.html: Oh that my people had hearkened unto me, and Israel had walked in my ways!
verses.text: Oh that my people had hearkened unto me, and Israel had walked in my ways!

verses.html: I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries.
verses.text: I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries.

verses.html: The haters of the LORD should have submitted themselves unto him: but their time should have endured for ever.
verses.text: The haters of the LORD should have submitted themselves unto him: but their time should have endured for ever.

verses.html: He should have fed them also with the finest of the wheat: and with honey out of the rock should I have satisfied thee.
verses.text: He should have fed them also with the finest of the wheat: and with honey out of the rock should I have satisfied thee.
